column1: # Syntax corpus of the postgresql language: one statement per line, tab separated. The accept and reject differential of the
# grammar (issue #3) and of the answer parity harness (issue #2). The parser tests read it through
# com.arcadedb.query.postgresql.corpus.Corpus, the harness (class PgParityIT of the e2e module) reads and regenerates it.
# Columns (the line after these comments names them):
#   id         a name that is stable across regenerations, unique; add a case at the end, never renumber or reuse an id
#   pg18       what PostgreSQL 18 does with the statement in its parser, as the harness reads it from a real server (the
#              statement is parsed and described, never run):
#                ok                     the grammar accepts it (the server answers, or fails after parsing, for example
#                                       with an undefined table, which is not a syntax matter)
#                pending-server         not asked of a server yet: add a case with this value and run the generator
#   subset     the recorded verdict of the parser, required for every entry: inside (the supported subset covers the syntax, it
#              must parse), outside (it does not, it must be refused with 0A000), error (PostgreSQL refuses the text itself, a
#              syntax error or an invalid escape, and the parser must refuse it with that SQLSTATE). inside is about the syntax
#              only: a statement that parses can still be refused when its names and types are bound
#   gap        - when the parser agrees with the two columns before, otherwise a short reason. A gap is a known disagreement:
#              the test fails when a statement marked as a gap starts to agree, so the list can only shrink
#   statement  the text, with backslash, tab, carriage return and newline written as \\, \t, \r and \n
#   source     where the statement comes from: written for the parser, s3 (written for the parity corpus), or the test of
#              PostgreSQL it was taken from, with the line
#   detail     the SQLSTATE the server answered when it parsed and described the statement, - when it accepted it without
#              an error. ok with 42P01 means: parsed, then refused by a later stage (an undefined table), so not a syntax matter
# The entries with an id of the form <test>:<line> are the SELECT shaped statements of the regression tests of PostgreSQL
# REL_18_7 (src/test/regress/sql), copyright PostgreSQL Global Development Group, PostgreSQL License. They were first read with
# their pg18 value from the expected output of the same test (src/test/regress/expected), the output of a real server that
# pg_regress compares against. The generator (the harness, issue #2) now asks the server of the harness for every entry and
# writes the pg18 and detail columns; the server runs with the C collation and the UTF8 encoding, and the version string,
# collation and encoding of the server that wrote them are the # server:, # collation: and # encoding: lines below.
# Licences: the statements taken from the tests of PostgreSQL (the entries with an id of the form <test>:<line>) are under the
# PostgreSQL License, and ATTRIBUTIONS.md has its notice. Everything else in this file is under the Apache License 2.0.
